brief.title: Bargaining over price (markets and small shops) — Vegetable Seller (A1)

functions.name: Bargain over a price politely (informal negotiation)
State a price and answer price questions

exponents: Can you give me a better price?
L0|CFN-0087|A1.notes: Use a polite question to request a lower price or a short statement to offer one.

L0|CFN-0085|A1.notes: State the price and make clear whether it is for one item or several.

L0|CFN-0020|A1.notes: Use a brief refusal with a polite word and a calm tone.

L1|STM-0020.description: A customer asks for a lower price. The seller states the current price, considers the request within their authority, and accepts an offer or declines politely. The exchange ends with a clear agreed price or a respectful decision not to buy.
flow: Establish the item, quantity and current price.
Offer an available price or decline politely.
Confirm the agreed price or close without a sale.
variationPoints: Whether bargaining is appropriate in the setting.
The seller's authority to change the price.
Short A1 exchanges or fuller explanations at higher CEFR levels.

L2|CM-03.summary: Support a buying decision through clear, respectful communication. Establish what the customer needs, explain relevant options and prices, respond to questions or objections, and confirm the customer's choice. Distinguish available offers from requests that need authorisation. Good selling helps the customer understand the options and next step without pressure or unsupported claims.

communicationMoves.move: Welcome the customer and open the exchange.
Ask questions to understand the customer's needs.
Describe and compare relevant options.
Explain the price and respond to concerns.
Discuss an available alternative or offer within the worker's authority.
Confirm the customer's chosen option and close respectfully.
Follow up on an earlier enquiry when appropriate.

qualityCriteria: Recommendations respond to the customer's stated needs.
Prices and included items are explained clearly.
Claims are supported by available information.
The customer can decline without pressure.
The chosen option and next step are understood.

responsibilities: Invite customers to ask about available items.
Explain prices and requested quantities clearly.
Respond politely to requests for a lower price.
Clarify the amount or measure supplied.
Confirm payment, change and the transaction outcome.
Recognise returning customers and invite them back respectfully.

jobKnowledge.title: Selling unit
jobKnowledge.text: The price may apply to an individual item, a group or a measured amount. The vendor's English should make that unit clear so the customer understands what the stated price covers.

jobKnowledge.title: Price flexibility
jobKnowledge.text: An available selling price and a customer's proposed price are different pieces of information. The vendor can explain an offer or decline it without inventing a discount or implying that bargaining is always available.

jobKnowledge.title: Transaction details
jobKnowledge.text: An exchange may involve cash, UPI or another available method. Communication distinguishes the amount due, the payment result and any change. It does not prescribe payment-system procedures.

jobKnowledge.title: Returning customers
jobKnowledge.text: A returning customer may refer to an earlier purchase. The vendor can clarify the current request without assuming that today's stock, amount or price is unchanged.

responsibilities: Name the requested vegetable or clarify which variety is wanted.
Explain differences between available sizes or varieties using observable descriptions.
Clarify whether the customer wants a piece count or a measured weight.
Offer an available substitute when the requested vegetable or quantity is unavailable.
Confirm mixed-item selections before calculating their separate amounts.

jobKnowledge.title: Produce identification
jobKnowledge.text: Customers may use different names for the same vegetable or ask for a particular variety. The seller can clarify by pointing to or describing the available produce without claiming that unfamiliar names are interchangeable.

jobKnowledge.title: Count and weight
jobKnowledge.text: A request for two pieces is different from a request for two kilos. The seller's language should confirm the vegetable and requested unit together, especially when an order contains several items.

jobKnowledge.title: Observable condition
jobKnowledge.text: Size, colour and visible condition can be described directly. Avoid unsupported claims about health benefits, chemical treatment or quality certification.

jobKnowledge.title: Substitutions
jobKnowledge.text: When the requested item is unavailable, the seller can describe an available alternative and ask whether the customer wants it. A substitution remains a customer choice.

deltaFromParent: Adds vegetable and variety identification to the parent vendor core.
Adds produce-specific descriptions without unsupported quality claims.
Adds clarification of piece-count versus weight-based produce requests.
Adds customer-approved substitutions and mixed-vegetable order clarification.

brief.title: Discussing quantity, weight and measures — Vegetable Seller (A1)

functions.name: Ask and answer about quantity, weight, size and measures

exponents: Do you want a small one?
L0|CFN-0086|A1.notes: Use how many for countable items and how much for an amount or weight.

L1|STM-0021.description: A customer and seller clarify how much of an item is wanted. They distinguish item count from weight, size or another measure and confirm the quantity before the transaction continues.
flow: Ask which item and quantity the customer wants.
Clarify the unit of measure or size.
State the available or measured quantity.
Confirm the quantity the customer accepts.
variationPoints: Counting items versus discussing weight, volume or length.
Available sizes and units used in the setting.
Whether the seller can supply the exact requested quantity.
Language length and clarification support by CEFR level.

brief.title: Taking payment (cash, UPI, card) — Vegetable Seller (A1)

functions.name: Take payment and give change or a receipt (cash, UPI, card)

L0|CFN-0089|A1.notes: State the amount and use the payment or change phrase that fits the transaction.

L1|STM-0034.description: A worker and customer complete a payment exchange. They confirm the amount, discuss an available payment method, and acknowledge the payment result. Where relevant, they confirm change or a receipt without presenting an unconfirmed payment as successful.
flow: Confirm the customer's payment method from the available options.
Check and communicate the known payment result.
Confirm any change or receipt and close the exchange.
variationPoints: Which payment methods the workplace actually accepts.
Whether a receipt is available or requested.
Simple spoken amounts or fuller explanations by CEFR level.

L2|CM-04.summary: Complete the communication around a transaction accurately. Confirm the agreed order or amount, explain the available payment options, acknowledge the known payment result, and clarify any change or receipt. If payment information is unclear or a problem occurs, check the relevant facts and explain who can resolve it. This module teaches transaction language rather than financial advice or payment-system procedures.

communicationMoves.move: Confirm the agreed order and total.
Discuss an available payment method.
Clarify an unclear amount or payment detail.
Acknowledge the known payment result and any change or receipt.
Explain a payment problem or refer it to the appropriate person.
Close the transaction politely.

qualityCriteria: The amount matches the agreed transaction.
Available methods are distinguished from unavailable options.
Payment is not described as complete without confirmation.
Any change or receipt is communicated accurately.
Unresolved problems are explained without unsupported promises.

pilot.purpose: Architecture-validation prototype approved by the author on 4 October 2026. Not for publication. Final state may never be COMPILED or PUBLISHED.

policies.D-U11: Job knowledge only to make communication realistic; not certification. No invented safety instructions, public procedures or legal/medical/financial advice. Factual claims in regulated areas must be traceable; U-1 avoids them.
policies.D-U12: Hybrid characters: role-specific realistic characters and reusable stakeholder archetypes; no single permanent character; Arif is not used.
policies.D-U14: Learning cycle for new role content: Context → Notice → Understand → Guided Practice → Role Practice → Performance Task → Feedback → Review/Retrieval. Not claimed to exist in the current book.
policies.D-U07: Vocabulary: propose terms only; the repository assigns V-<SCOPE>-<NUMBER> codes and reuses existing codes. Never invent codes.
policies.D-U10: Generate only the requested delta. Do not regenerate objects supplied in context.

style.currency: Indian rupees (₹) unless the situation requires otherwise
style.names: realistic South Asian names by default; international names where the context has them; no stereotypes
style.brands: no real company or brand names; use generic descriptions (e.g. 'the delivery app', 'the dealership')
style.languages: English only. No Bengali or Hindi script or transliteration in U-1.
style.audio: None. Content must be fully usable as text (D-U06).

context.review: Output is stored as GENERATED, then AI QA, then Editorial Review by the author. Specialist and native review are NOT_REQUIRED for U-1. It is never published.
